title: Prompt playbook scratchpad — extraction & persona experiments
content:
Purpose / quick note to self:
- Scratchpad for prompt templates, few-shot sets, and observed failure modes while prototyping the prompt library for product demos and customer playbooks.
- Keep this informal: raw examples, metrics, oddball cases. Will move polished ones to the repo / confluence later.

Design goals / heuristics I'm using: 
- Be explicit about output format: JSON blocks or TSV for downstream parsers.
- Few-shot examples should be short (2-4 shots) and target the tricky edge-cases we care about.
- Encourage the model to say "I don't know" rather than hallucinate by including negative examples.
- Use stop sequences and token limits for cost control on long-form tasks.

Common meta-template (use when experimenting):
System: You are a concise assistant optimized for structured extraction. Always output valid JSON and nothing else.
User: {TASK_DESCRIPTION}
Input: {RAW_TEXT}
Output schema: {SCHEMA}
Shots: [positive example(s), negative example(s) when helpful]
Config notes: temperature=0.0-0.2 for extraction; max_tokens small (50-180); stop=["\n\n"] or a closing curly.

=== Entity extraction (customer support tickets) ===
Goal: extract intent, product, urgency, and named entities + confidence.
Schema: {"intent": "string","product": "string|null","urgency": "low|medium|high","entities": [{"type":"string","text":"string"}], "extraction_confidence": "0-1"}

Prompt (few-shot):
System: You are a JSON-only extractor.
User: Extract fields from the ticket.
Input: "My Titan instance keeps crashing when I upload a 2GB file; I need this fixed asap. - Maya Patel"
Output: {"intent":"crash_report","product":"Titan","urgency":"high","entities":[{"type":"file_size","text":"2GB"},{"type":"person","text":"Maya Patel"}],"extraction_confidence":"0.92"}

User: Input: "I keep getting a permission denied error trying to pull embeddings. Not urgent, just blocked. - ops team"
Output: {"intent":"access_error","product":"embeddings","urgency":"medium","entities":[{"type":"team","text":"ops"}],"extraction_confidence":"0.78"}

Notes / failure cases: 
- Model sometimes invents product names when not present (hallucination). Counter: include shot where product is absent and output must be null.
- Confidence calibration: inline "extraction_confidence" from heuristics (overfit to examples) is brittle. Consider returning token-level annotations instead for training.

=== Persona-driven assistant (product marketing tone) ===
Task: rewrite a short feature blurb in a more customer-friendly voice with a hint of urgency but no hyperbole.
Prompt template:
System: You are an empathetic product writer for developer audiences. Avoid marketing hyperbole.
User: Rewrite the following: 
---
{ORIGINAL_TEXT}
---
Constraints: 1) Max 60 words. 2) Keep technical accuracy. 3) Add one sentence about developer time saved.

Few-shot examples:
Shot1: Original: "Our API now supports 2x throughput with new batching"
Rewrite: "New batching doubles throughput, helping engineers process more requests without extra infra time—cutting integration time by hours per week."

Shot2 (negative): Original: "This is the best API, fastest in the world!"
Rewrite: "[REFUSE] The original contains unsupported claims. Ask for benchmark data or provide neutral phrasing"

Failure modes noticed: 
- Model typically adds confident but unverifiable claims ("2x faster for all workloads"). Force neutral language or include a bracketed refusal pattern.
- When prompts include too many constraints, model drops the 'time saved' sentence. Tradeoff: loosen length constraint to allow required sentence.

=== Few-shot set: extract structured action items from meeting notes ===
Schema: [{"owner":"string","action":"string","due":"YYYY-MM-DD|null","priority":"low|med|high"}]
Prompt (shots):
- Note fragment: "Jordan: follow up with infra team about quota" -> {owner:"Jordan",action:"follow up with infra team about quota",due:null,priority:"med"}
- Note fragment: "Deliver rollout checklist by 2025-08-01 - Priya" -> {owner:"Priya",action:"Deliver rollout checklist",due:"2025-08-01",priority:"high"}

Observation: small list outputs are stable; long noisy meeting transcripts produce hallucinated due dates. Add explicit negative example: "No date mentioned => due:null".

=== Prompt for QA / summarization with tool/function-calling style ===
Goal: produce 3-bullet summary + list of open questions.
Prompt: system: You are a terse meeting summarizer. Output only JSON with fields: summary (list of 3 strings), open_questions (list).
Input sample: [paste transcript chunk]
Shots: show example where transcript includes an unanswered question and one where all questions were resolved.
Config: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 320.

=== Weird failure cases collected (raw) ===
Case A: "short ambiguous input" -> model invents extra context.
Example:
Input: "Ticket: latency spike"
Bad output: {"intent":"performance_issue","product":"TitanDb","urgency":"high"} // TitanDb not mentioned
Fix tried: add explicit constraint: "If product not mentioned, set product:null and explain reason in a separate 'notes' field." That reduced hallucination but increased verbosity.

Case B: "Multi-turn persona leak" -> model repeats system instruction in user output.
Example: when streaming, header lines from system appear at response start. Probable cause: system prompt included sample outputs. Fix: strip samples from streaming channel or use function-calling for structured outputs.

=== Quick experiment log (latest runs) ===
Date: 2025-07-28
Task: entity extraction (tickets)
Model variants: redwood-lite-1, redwood-pro-2
Config: temp=0.0, max_tokens=120, stop=["\n\n"]
Dataset: 250 dev tickets (internal)
Metrics (approx):
- redwood-lite-1: exact-match 0.62, F1 0.74, avg latency 110ms
- redwood-pro-2: exact-match 0.72, F1 0.83, avg latency 210ms
Notes: pro model improves recall on person+team extraction but still fakes product when dataset lacks explicit product mentions.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Add calibrated 'refusal' shot to all few-shot sets where model must output null / refuse when uncertain. (action: add 2 negative examples)
- Try function-calling style API for extraction to reduce formatting errors (PR in GH linked above).
- Build a small evaluation harness that measures hallucination rate specifically for product field (JIRA:DX-412).
- Talk to Jordan about publishing a trimmed playbook for Solutions Eng. (Slack pinged)

Notes to self (quick tips):
- Use 0.0-0.2 temp for structured tasks; prefer 0.0 for anything deterministic.
- Add explicit tokens like "### END" or stop sequences to prevent rambling.
- When training prompting guidelines for customers, include examples of how to ask for exact JSON only.

Random prompt snippets I've been saving: 
- "Extract code snippets from the text. Return an array of strings where each string is the code block without markdown."
- "Rewrite this email as a short apology (1-2 sentences) and include suggested next steps."
- "Given the error log, return the most likely root cause (one sentence) and up to three remediation steps."

Questions / for later: 
- Is there a standard token budget guideline we want to recommend for example prompts in the playbook? (ask product)
- Should we include latency expectations per example in the public examples? Risk: might change with model versions.

End of scratchpad.

-- Alex
(PS: if this grows, migrate good examples to repo/examples/prompt-playbook and link to confluence.)
